Do you have ten to fifteen minutes?' — frames availability and 10-15 min window but does not explicitly promise a 'quote you can depend on' and does not wait for clear yes before diving into details.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Not asked. Jules moves directly to logistics probing ('what date are you looking into moving?') with no inquiry about concerns or what answers the customer wants on the call.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (apartment), floor/stories (4th floor with elevator, moving to 2nd floor without), number of rooms (2-bedroom), walking distance/route (4 miles). Not fully covered: special considerations (washer/dryer mentioned as possible item to move themselves but not detailed), additional rooms, additional stops. Partial.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Yes — 'do you need help packing with the boxes?' Customer declined.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes — 'How many boxes do you think there's gonna be like a rough number?' Customer answered '25 maybe.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full — Jules provides typical range: 'we would just take anywhere from three to four hours with an estimated cost of $654 to $872' and personalizes to the move specifics (4th floor with elevator to 2nd floor without).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full — discloses no fees upfront ('we do not have any additional fees, you know, we don't have anything like if you will fee, no disassemble, reassembly fees, no hidden fees at all') and explains 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments ('we have a minimum of two and a half hours and then after that, the time is prorated in fifteen minute increments').
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After delivering the estimate, Jules does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent, and does not hold silence for customer reaction. Customer volunteers 'Okay. Alright, thank you' but Jules never solicited or confirmed this.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No — no summary of promises or check-back on concerns, since no concerns were raised and no promises were delivered.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Jules does not ask 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent. Conversation ends with customer saying they will shop other quotes.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Jules does not ask 'Would you like our help with your move?' or similar. Jules only says 'whenever you're ready to get this scheduled feel free to give us a callback' — a passive redirect without a direct ask.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: None. No booking is confirmed. Jules provides no date/time confirmation, no phone confirmation, no arrival window confirmation, no crew size, no address re-confirmation, and no notes left for crew.

top_strength: Jules gathered all four discovery basics (name, moving day, route, approximate size) early and cleanly, and provided a well-anchored, personalized estimate with full transparency on fees and minimum billing.
coaching_note: Jules skipped the entire Section 2 (Their Concerns) discovery — never asked what the customer's biggest concerns or questions were — which is the foundation for the whole call; he also abandoned Sections 5, 6, and 7 (Two Promises, Concerns Again, Ask for the Business) entirely, letting the customer walk out without hearing the guarantees, a final concerns check, or an explicit ask to book.
